readings.core_relation: DMD pairs synthesized views at perturbed wrist-camera poses with transforms toward later expert poses. This adds corrective recovery supervision, not just visual diversity, and avoids backward commands when perturbations overshoot the next demonstrated pose.

readings.core_relation: Without ensembling, 100-action chunks raise ACT success from 1% to 44%; longer chunks worsen it. Removing variational training drops human-data success from 35.3% to 2% but scarcely changes scripted results. Separately tuned ensembling helps ACT by 3.3 points but hurts VINN.
readings.scope: Two simulated tasks. Six participants thread in 20 versus 33 seconds at 50 versus 5 Hz leader updates; followers remain at 50 Hz. Autonomous threading succeeds only 20% despite 100 demonstrations, exposing visual-localization difficulties.

readings.core_relation: ALOHA offers affordable, directly joint-coupled teleoperation; ACT learns joint-target chunks, ensembles same-time predictions for frequent feedback, and models human variability. Together they support precise bimanual imitation: bag opening reaches 88% and battery insertion 96%, versus zero final-stage success for four tuned baselines.
readings.scope: Two simulated and six physical tasks; $20,000 budget; 50 demonstrations/physical task, 100 for threading; one seed, 25 physical trials/task. Threading succeeds only 20%. Six participants work faster at 50 than 5 Hz.

readings.core_relation: DMD pairs synthesized off-trajectory wrist views with actions toward later expert poses, supplying recovery supervision and avoiding backward commands after overshoot. Improvements span regression and diffusion policies, beyond scarce task data.
readings.scope: Adaptation uses task data, play, or both. Tests include pushing, stacking, pouring, hanging, and cup arrangement.
